title: Murine Transient Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion Model with Drug Delivery
author: Lee, Murphy, et al.
materials: This section describes the pre-operative preparation for mice to undergo the tMCAO surgery.1.Weigh the animal and transfer it to an anesthesia induction box. Anesthetize the animal at 5 (v/v) % isoflurane delivered with 1.5 L O2/min.2.Once the animal is anesthetized (check paw pinch and ocular reflex), transfer the animal to a heat plate and insert a rectal thermometer to monitor and maintain body temperature at 37 °C.Note: No other physiological monitoring e.g. blood pressure, blood gas analysis was performed.3.Maintain anesthesia with 1.5% isoflurane delivered by a face mask.4.Administer 100 μl buprenorphine (dilute Buprevet 0.3 mg/mL 1:10 in sterilized water)subcutaneously for analgesia.Note: The appropriate analgesia may be dependent on your protocol and experimental design.5.Shave the ventral area of the neck as well as the area between the left eye and ear. The latter is for the attachment of the Doppler probe.6.Apply eye ointment to avoid eye dryness during operation.7.Once all necessary pre-operative preparation has been completed, transfer the animal to the operating bench with a heating pad controlled by a rectal probe and anesthesia face mask.Note: In our set up, the pre-operative bench is separate from the operating bench.

steps.title: Prepare workspace and catheter
steps.instruction: Prepare a sterilized aseptic workspace; create an infusion catheter by inserting a thin polyimide catheter through a needle tip, glue it in place, allow the glue to set, attach the needle to a 1 mL syringe, flush the catheter with water to verify no leakage; sterilize the catheter with 70 % ethanol; set up the operating area, arrange all surgical tools and ensure all surfaces and tools are sterilized.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia and monitor temperature
steps.instruction: Weigh the mouse, place it in an induction box and anesthetize with 5 % (v/v) isoflurane delivered in 1.5 L O₂/min; confirm anesthesia by lack of paw pinch and ocular reflex; transfer to a heated plate, insert a rectal thermometer and maintain body temperature at 37 °C; maintain anesthesia with 1.5 % isoflurane via a face mask.

steps.title: Administer analgesia and prep site
steps.instruction: Inject 100 µL buprenorphine (prepared by diluting Buprevet 0.3 mg/mL 1:10 in sterile water) subcutaneously; shave the ventral neck and the area between the left eye and ear; apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes.

steps.title: Transfer to operating bench
steps.instruction: Move the anesthetized mouse to the operating bench equipped with a heating pad controlled by the rectal probe and an anesthesia face mask.

steps.title: Expose carotid arteries
steps.instruction: Place the mouse supine and tape its forelegs to the operating surface; make a small incision slightly right of the midline on the neck; separate fascia, retract skin and salivary glands to expose the common carotid artery (CCA), internal carotid artery (ICA), and external carotid artery (ECA) while avoiding damage to the vagus nerve.

steps.title: Place sutures on arteries
steps.instruction: Wrap two 6‑0 nylon sutures loosely around the CCA and one around the ECA; tighten the ECA suture and the lower (proximal) CCA suture, positioning the proximal suture as low as possible to create space for the infusion catheter.

steps.title: Clamp ICA and incise CCA
steps.instruction: Apply a vascular clamp to the ICA; make a small incision on the CCA near the proximal suture, keeping the incision low to maximize the length between incision and clamp.

steps.title: Insert filament and secure
steps.instruction: Insert the endovascular filament (coating length 2–3 mm, tip diameter 0.22 mm) into the CCA through the incision and secure it with the distal CCA suture.

steps.title: Advance filament to MCA
steps.instruction: Remove the ICA clamp and gently advance the filament through the ICA toward the MCA to a depth of 8–10 mm (or until slight resistance is felt), confirming placement by changes in laser‑Doppler flow (LDF).

steps.title: Confirm occlusion and maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Observe a sharp, sudden decline in LDF indicating a ≥70 % reduction in cerebral blood flow relative to baseline; exclude any animal not meeting this criterion; maintain anesthesia throughout the occlusion period (30 min) as required by the experimental design.
